Q2.dialect_note_md: In MySQL, `LIMIT … OFFSET` is allowed inside a scalar subquery, but not inside `IN (…)`, `ANY`, `ALL` or `SOME`.

Q3.dialect_note_md: MySQL's default collation (`utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`) compares strings case-insensitively, so letter case alone won't split a group the way it does in PostgreSQL. Surrounding spaces still count. To see the case-sensitive behaviour, try `GROUP BY BINARY email`.

Q4.dialect_note_md: MySQL rejects a `DELETE` whose subquery reads the same table (error 1093). Workbench's safe-update mode may block the delete (error 1175): run `SET SQL_SAFE_UPDATES = 0;` first. Re-run `setup.sql` afterwards to restore the data.

Q6.dialect_note_md: MySQL prints zero spend as `0.00` where the expected output shows `0` — same value.

Q17.dialect_note_md: In MySQL, subtracting one date from another does not give a day count.

Q19.dialect_note_md: In MySQL, `date - integer` does not subtract days.

Q20.dialect_note_md: MySQL has no `PERCENTILE_CONT` or `MEDIAN`, so only the second part of the question applies.

Q27.dialect_note_md: MySQL trap: `first_date + 30` is not 30 days later — MySQL turns the date into the number 20250103 and adds 30.

Q28.dialect_note_md: MySQL has no `generate_series` — see the hint.

Q30.dialect_note_md: In MySQL, `||` means OR, not string concatenation. A recursive CTE also sizes its text columns from the anchor row, so longer paths can fail with "Data too long".
